name: ChronoWeave
adaptations: All requests keep the original title and prompt from tracks/chronoweave.json verbatim; each adds a human-sounding motivation and a precise 'What I need' public contract (endpoints, JSON shapes, validation, error codes, ordering and tie-break rules, exact algorithms where numbers are asserted). Architectural-pressure notes from the specification are not shown to agents.

Times are integers (seconds on a shared clock) and transaction time is client-supplied but monotonic per ledger (409 clock_regression on regression, equal allowed), so historical reads are deterministic and testable; the README defines canonical JSON once for every hash, MAC and comparison.

Request 0: 'speculative branch forking' is a frozen copy of main at fork time (branches see nothing written to main afterwards); retraction is a main-only tombstone write; the canonical order is (effective_at, asserted_at, record order) so the pre-P1 tie-break is explicit and testable; SQLite under CHRONOWEAVE_DATA_DIR provides the persistence.

Request 1: 'insulated by a checkpoint' is an explicit checkpoint write; taint is derived as of a knowledge time (never stored by reads), and a reconcile write was added so that 'pending reconcile' has a defined exit.

Request 2: 'cryptographic epoch seals' -> SHA-256 seal digest over the sealed interval's assertions; the 'OverrideAuthority proof' -> HMAC-SHA256 with an authority secret supplied via PUT /api/authority (no asymmetric crypto library is available offline).

Request 3: the 'three-way causal merge' in the title is defined as promotion (merge) into main with conflicts = keys changed on both sides since the fork; promoted copies take the merge's asserted_at; merges respect seals and refuse id collisions atomically.

Request 4: rules are explicit requires/unless conditions on keys; CompensationObligation records are emitted for each maximal effective-time interval that a write to main removes from where a rule held.

Request 5 (CI): reuses Switchboard request 6's ci.json selector contract verbatim in substance (safe, cheap, docs-only -> nothing, pyproject.toml/uv.lock/ci.json -> ALL, < 10 s, targets must exist); the original '<1s' target is kept as guidance for the selected component tests ('about a second') but is not asserted; ci_from_step is 5.

Request 6: conflict resolution chooses a winning side per conflicting key; LastAssertionWins, CausalDepthPriority and QuorumWitnessResolver have exact definitions (quorum witnesses = distinct nodes asserting the candidate's value on that side) and are discoverable via GET /api/resolvers.

Request 7 (P1): 'deterministic BLAKE2b payload digest' -> hashlib.blake2b(digest_size=32) over the canonical JSON of {id, key, value, author, node, causal_parents}; larger digest wins and the rule applies everywhere canonical order or merge candidates are used, including already-recorded history. Earlier-step hidden tests only assert the old insertion-order tie-break before step 7.

Request 8: tenant_id travels in an X-Tenant header (default tenant when absent); assertion byte budgets count the canonical JSON of values on main plus own assertions of active branches; DELETE /api/branches/{name} (discard) was added so branch budgets can be released.

Request 9: the four verifiers are configured per tenant through one settings API, run on every assertion entering main (direct or merged) in name order, and have exact, simple, testable rules and rejection codes.

Request 10: zstd -> gzip from the standard library (mtime 0 for byte-identical exports); the bundle is self-contained (slice plus causal ancestors) and verification/import check only the file's own content.

Request 11: a 'grant' is an assertion with key prefix grant: and value {payee, amount}; fees are marginal tiered brackets configured per tenant; '30 days later' is the late threshold (fees not refunded); rounding is half-up to cents.

Request 12: compaction is defined so that it never changes any read (historical repeatability, INV-CW-01); compacted intervals become read-only and compacted assertions insulate later taint like checkpoints; branches forked before compaction keep working.

Request 13: webhooks and event sinks -> HTTP POSTs to sink URLs registered via the API (the hidden suite points them at its fake external service); idempotency key = SHA-256 of the canonical body; HMAC-SHA256 signature; fixed retry schedule; delivery must not delay writes. A 'sealed grant' reuses request 11's grant: assertions inside a seal.

Request 14 (P2): 'concurrently retracted parent' is made deterministic: a promotion is poisoned when an assertion it would promote would be tainted on main by a retraction the branch did not inherit; the merge is aborted atomically, a QuarantineReceipt is recorded and the branch is closed as quarantined. Before step 14 such promotions went through and came out tainted; no earlier hidden test exercises that case.

Request 15: the query mini-language has a published grammar (AS OF, EFFECTIVE BETWEEN, WHERE with AND/OR/NOT, KEY/AUTHOR/NODE/STATUS/TAINTED [BY author:x]/DESCENDS FROM); errors are 422 query_syntax with an offset; hostile input must never execute.

Request 16: the external authority oracle -> a fake quorum service under CHRONOWEAVE_EXTERNAL_URL (/authority/v1/tenants/{tenant}/certify); witness overrides complement request 2's HMAC proofs; per-tenant breaker (threshold/cooldown configurable for testing, 2 s call timeout); 'degraded read-only mode' means reads and witness-free writes continue while witness checks rely on cached quorum certificates or fail with 503 authority_unavailable.

Request 17: the five regional policies are additional verifiers in request 9's family, applying to pii:<region>:<subject>:<field> keys, with a residency rule and a full or forward right-to-erasure rule driven by erasure:<region>:<subject> assertions; extension isolation is measured by the harness (files edited, CI selection), never by hidden tests.

Request 18: 'zero-knowledge' -> salted SHA-256 commitments (no ZK library offline); roles via an X-Role header (owner/auditor); auditors see only a redacted graph and a stateless verifier, and nothing an auditor receives may contain ids, keys, values, authors or nodes.

Request 19: MCP & HTTP parity -> a minimal MCP-like JSON-RPC 2.0 server over newline-delimited stdio (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) started with '.venv/bin/python -m chronoweave mcp', plus a CLI '.venv/bin/python -m chronoweave cli <operation> --args <json>'; nine read-only operations (inspection, branch simulation via a new POST /api/simulate, audit export as base64) must return exactly the HTTP JSON bodies and error envelopes.

Request 20 (P3): a diamond is explicitly valid; the injected invalid cycle is an assertion listing its own id as a parent (previously 422 unknown_parent, now 422 causal_cycle) and any parent cycle inside an imported or verified bundle (422 causal_cycle, checked right after the digest). A lineage endpoint was added so that silent loss of compacted lineage is observable; the diamond/compaction/retraction race is exercised end to end (taint once per retraction, one grant.invalidated per grant, quarantine of the late branch, compaction summaries and seal verification untouched).

Hidden tests are black-box: HTTP against the service launched from the candidate's run.json with a fresh CHRONOWEAVE_DATA_DIR per app fixture, plus subprocess stdio/CLI for request 19; DRIFT_STEP only selects the P1/P2/P3 era expectations.

Inline probe requests 7, 14 and 20 drop the draft's 'Fault Probe Pn:' title prefix and 'PROBE Pn:' prompt prefix so agents are not told which requests are measured; the rest of each title and prompt is verbatim.
